title: responses-v2beta: compatibility shim for determinism flags, streaming metadata proxy, and toolcall stability
author: Sophie Liao
description: Context: OpenAI recently shipped a responses-v2beta surface with explicit determinism controls (seed + deterministic hints) and a slight rework of streaming event shapes to better support tool calls and structured outputs. Motivation: downstream Redwood users expect parity between our OpenAI compatibility adapter and our native Responses surface (hosted/dedicated/private). This PR implements a compatibility shim that preserves determinism flags during routing, proxies arbitrary metadata fields through streaming events, and stabilizes tool/function-call boundaries so reassembly and callback handling remain deterministic across retries and fallbacks. Summary of changes: 1) Adapter layer: api/compat/responses_v2beta_adapter.go maps responses-v2beta fields to internal request model, forwarding seed and deterministic_hint fields when present. 2) Streaming layer: bridge/streaming/reassembly.go now tags every streamed fragment with a canonical event-index and, when supplied, the seed/determinism annotation to ensure consistent reassembly and replay equivalence. 3) Metadata passthrough: streaming events and websocket proxies carry a metadata map (opaque string->string) and attach it to final response records; we preserve nested tool_call.metadata as a flattened prefixed map to avoid subtle JSON schema mismatches in consumer SDKs. 4) Tool/function call stability: improved delimiting rules for tool-invocation start/end events, and added heuristic to coalesce partial tool payload frames when connection jitter is detected. 5) Backwards compatibility: when head model does not support determinism flags, adapter drops them but emits an info log and metric (compat.determinism.dropped) for visibility. 6) Docs & SDK: python and typescript SDK adapters were updated to surface the new deterministic flags and metadata passthrough in their Response wrappers. 7) Tests: unit coverage added for adapter mapping, streaming reassembly deterministic replay, and an integration canary that runs against a responses-v2beta mock with jitter-injection. Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature-flag openai.v2beta_compat; will enable for 10% of traffic for 48h then ramp to 100% provided no regressions in canary metrics (latency, errors, determinism_regressions). Checklist: - [x] Adapter mapping implemented - [x] Streaming reassembly deterministic tagging - [x] Metadata passthrough format decided and implemented - [x] SDK updates included - [x] Tests (unit + integration canary) - [x] Docs updated (docs/openai_responses_v2beta_compat.md) - [x] Metrics added (compat.determinism.dropped, streaming.reassembly.latency)

review_comments: Miguel Ortega: Can we guarantee that seed propagation doesn't change request fingerprinting? If not, we should gate metric emission behind a config flag.
Sophie Liao: Seed is only forwarded to models that declare support; in other cases we add a metric but keep request fingerprinting identical. Added unit tests to assert fingerprint parity.
Priya Raman: The flattened metadata prefixing approach seems fine, but please add an example to the docs showing how nested tool metadata is surfaced in SDKs.
Sophie Liao: Added examples in docs/openai_responses_v2beta_compat.md and SDK tests to demonstrate the flattened form.
Evan Schultz: Performance question: does adding event_index and seed_hint to every fragment increase payload size significantly? Run perf-canary with representative traffic.

Sophie Liao: Measured ~0.6% median token payload increase in perf-canary at 95th percentile throughput. Added metric streaming.reassembly.byte_overhead and a configurable toggle to drop seed_hint on high-throughput routes.
release_notes: Compatibility shim for Responses v2beta: forwards seed/determinism hints when supported, proxies metadata through streaming events, stabilizes tool/function call frame boundaries for reliable reassembly. Opt-in behind feature flag openai.v2beta_compat. Includes SDK and docs updates.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for adapter mapping and reassembly logic (coverage + core edge cases). Integration canary ran against a jitter-injection mock for 48 hours with 10% traffic; no determinism regressions observed. Performance canary ran at 95th percentile and showed ~0.6% payload overhead; throughput and latency SLOs held. CI status green with one flaky test retried and resolved.
rollback_plan: Disable feature flag openai.v2beta_compat to revert compatibility behavior immediately. If SDK regressions occur, rollback with a targeted server-side config change to drop metadata passthrough and revert adapter mapping. Postmortem checklist includes alerting on compat.determinism.dropped > 0.1% and streaming.reassembly.error_rate > 0.05%.
